settings.description: How many characters the fake provider sends in each piece of a streamed reply. Zero sends each block in one piece.
How long the fake provider waits before each piece of a streamed reply, so a chat in the test tenant streams at a speed a person can watch. Tests use no wait.
The most models one person's registry may hold. Adding one more is refused.
How many characters of text count as one token when Keystone estimates a call's size because the provider offers no count. Lower counts more tokens, which is the safe side.
The safety margin added to an estimated token count, as a percentage of it. A provider's own count gets no margin.
Tokens counted for each message in an estimate, for its role and framing, on top of its content.
Tokens counted for each tool offered in an estimate, on top of its name, description and schema.
Tokens counted for each image in an estimate, whatever its size.
Tokens counted in an estimate for a file that is named by reference, whose size the estimate cannot see.
How many times the Responses adapter sends a call again when it failed before any of the reply arrived and the failure is one that may pass. Zero sends each call once.
How long the Responses adapter waits before its first retry. The wait doubles with each retry.
The longest the Responses adapter waits before a retry. When the provider asks for a longer wait, the call fails at once so another model can be tried.
How long the Responses adapter waits for a reply to begin before it gives up on the call.
How long a streamed reply through the Responses adapter may send nothing before it is given up on.
The thinking budget, in tokens, from which the Responses adapter asks for medium reasoning effort. A smaller budget asks for low.
The thinking budget, in tokens, from which the Responses adapter asks for high reasoning effort.
